findings.reason: without naming the coordinator as the arm runner and the node as the analyser, the section's done-when is unmeetable by the worker it names and the verdict it exists to produce is never reached.
findings.text: the section's measure is a population of at least 90 local implement runs and 30 codex implement runs across five concurrent arms, which no single dispatched node can produce, and the section — unlike §7, which says its live check "is dispatched by the coordinator after the node lands" and that "the section closes only on that run" — never says who runs the arms, so a node dispatched on §8 will either report a verdict on a population far below its own threshold or block having spent its turn

findings.reason: the control is the section's guard against reporting an unmeasured figure as zero, which §1 already identifies as the census's error; without an artifact the plan must say who records one and where, or the codex edit-failure metric cannot be reported either way.
findings.text: the codex positive control ("the edit-failure parser first finds the failure in a recorded stream known to contain a refused patch, so a zero for codex means zero and not an unread field") names no path, and no such stream exists: the only two files under `docs/research/fixtures/` are `codex-anchored-edit-stream.jsonl` and `omp-stream.jsonl`, and neither contains a `file_change` item or an `apply_patch` call, so the one control that decides whether the codex edit-failure metric is a real zero or an unread field cannot be run as written

findings.reason: the function is named (`_seed_worker_mcp_settings`, called through `seed_harness_home`) and it is the only call site, so a grep recovers it and the node's design is unchanged.
findings.text: §4 cites the settings seeder as "called from `reckon/_backends.py` near line 2383", but that call is at `reckon/_backends.py:2841` (`worker_mcp_servers=(_declared_worker_mcp_servers(fence_config) …)` inside `seed_harness_home`), and line 2383 sits inside token accounting for the observation path, so a reader following the pointer lands in unrelated code

findings.reason: the record field §8 splits the population on would then say the treatment was applied while the arm offered nothing, measuring a baseline that differs only in having lost `Edit` and `MultiEdit`, which reads as a token saving bought by failing more nodes.
findings.text: §4 declares that "the run home registers the `reckon-anchored-edit` server with `--root` set to the run's write roots" but names no file, and the only registration route its own evidence proves is the argv's `--mcp-config` with `--strict-mcp-config` (recorded in `docs/research/worker-steering-and-anchored-edit-prototypes.html`), while the seeder §4 points at (`_seed_worker_mcp_settings`, `reckon/_worker_fence.py:324`, reached only through the gate at `reckon/_worker_fence.py:274`) writes two permission keys, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` and `enabledMcpjsonServers`, and carries no server definition at all — so a node can register the server in a key no harness reads, and still record `anchored_edit: true` because its own seeder ran

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every href and cited file resolves (all extensionless hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`, the audit anchors `#s3-anchored-edit-tool` and `#s6-omp-headless-contract` exist), but the §4 citation of the settings-seeder's call site is wrong by roughly 460 lines.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's done-when asserts "at least 30 implement runs per local arm and 15 per codex arm" with no statement of who runs that population, unlike §7 which explicitly assigns its live check to the coordinator.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the measurement record lands on `docs/evidence/archive/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node-landed.html`, the fixtures on `docs/research/fixtures/`, and the §6 note on the crew reports directory; none is a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new identifiers are named by what they do (`anchored_edit`, `read_anchored`, `edit_anchored`, `omp-local`, `_within_any`), and no section, ticket or version label reaches a symbol, filename or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's arithmetic and §9's mechanism both hold and are verified against the tree, but §4 names no file the harness reads for the server registration it declares, while the only route its own §2 evidence proved is the argv's `--mcp-config`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (§4 one treatment arm's wiring, §8 one measurement and its verdict); §8's default-setting and removal clauses are the consequence of the single verdict it is scored on, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares s4←s3, s5←s3+s4, s7←s6 and s8←s4+s5+s7, which are exactly the waits the sections state in prose (§5 "this section waits on §4", §7 on §6, §8 on the three arms), and `plan-informs` resolves to `docs/plans/a-live-worker-can-be-reached.html`.
